text:
alex: heads-up — seeing a regression on the compactless batch path after the recent kernel-routing change. stress-run with paged-attn (blocksize=32) hit OOMs and a ~2.1x token-latency increase for long sequences. attaching quick notes and repro commands below.

alex: profile snapshot: 
- 90% requests routed to compactless kernel for seq>=512 (unexpected)
- peak GPU mem 34.7GB (baseline ~29.2GB)
- kv-cache churn spikes during repack/compaction window
- allocator free-list fragmentation much higher (many tiny slabs)

alex: repro (local repro harness):
```
# run stress driver
make run-stress SCENARIO=paged-attn-long SEQ=1024 BATCH=2 ITER=120
# collect nvprof + heaptrace
./collect-profiles --out=/tmp/run1 --nvprof --heap-snapshots
```

alex: logs (snip):
```
2026-02-28 14:21:02 WARN kernel-router: routed -> compactless (policy=latency-pref)
2026-02-28 14:21:02 INFO allocator: alloc 248MB slab id=0x7f2a free 12 -> 3
2026-02-28 14:21:04 ERROR runtime: OOM while allocating workspace for blockmgr
2026-02-28 14:21:04 INFO blockmgr: started compaction pass (cost_est=1.9)
```

maya: ugh, I saw something similar on canary yesterday but assumed it was batch-sig change. can you paste the kernel-routing snapshot?

alex: pasted above — routing policy is still `latency-pref`, but the decision matrix changed: we now prefer streaming-compactless for sequences where expected_kv_hits > 0.6. that heuristic overestimates for our long-paged-attn workload because kv cache misses trigger repack.

cheng: @alex great catch. likely two interacting problems: (1) routing pushes compactless which disables some buffer reuse paths, (2) allocator thresholds were lowered in #4021 so small-slab churn increased. either change alone would be okay, together they OOM.

sam: quick test idea: force-route those long sequences to `streaming-compact` (the other kernel) in the router and re-run the stress to see if mem and latency come down. that's a cheap canary.

alex: did that — rerun with `--force-kernel=streaming-compact` produced: peak mem 29.6GB, latency ~1.03x baseline. no OOMs.

linda: ok this sounds like a regression we should hotfix. priority P0 for dedicated infra perf regressions. can we do a rollback of the routing tweak and add more conservative thresholds?

cheng: proposing a two-step mitig:
1) revert kernel routing heuristic change (router config -> previous weights)
2) raise allocator coalescing threshold to 48KB and re-enable eager-reuse for blockmgr on compactless -> this should reduce fragmentation.

cheng: config snippet to test locally:
```
router:
  policy: latency-pref
  overrides:
    seq_ge_512: prefer=streaming-compact weight=0.85
allocator:
  coalesce_min_bytes: 49152
  eager_block_reuse: true
blockmgr:
  compaction_cost_limit: 2.5
```

maya: will run that locally and smoke test on canary. also adding a quick perf test that toggles `eager_block_reuse` to measure regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by linda for branch hotfix/reroute-2065 — env: canary, version: 0.23.1-hotfix. ETA: 6m

alex: note for postmortem — need better telemetry to show when routing moves a majority of seq-heavy traffic to a kernel that disables reuse. current dashboards show kernel mix but not reuse penalty.

sam: +1 on telemetry. maybe add a derived metric: "reuse_efficiency" = reused_bytes / total_allocated_bytes per-minute. would give an early warning before OOMs.

linda: assigning: cheng -> rollback + allocator tweak PR; maya -> canary smoke + perf smoke; alex -> add reuse_efficiency metric and attach the nvprof snapshots into the issue. I'll own the rollout. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — putting the nvprof/heap dumps in the issue now: https://redwood/infra/issue/INF-2065

maya: started test run on canary, will post results in thread. :eyes:

(emoji reactions: alex :rocket:, cheng :heavy_check_mark:, maya :eyes:)
